Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

law noun

also laws, the law, against the law, by law, statute, in accordance with the law, according to the law, pass a law, ratify a bill, reject a bill, spirit of the law, break the law, enforce the law, throw the book at someone

classical

Tac. Germ. 19.5: bonae lēgēs
Traupman 178, 179, 180, 195
Traupman 195: against the law, contrā lēgem; by law, lēge
Traupman 338

lēx, lēgis f.

noun, third declension

a law; in the plural, the laws

A particular law, passed by the people: lēgem ferre, to propose a law (Traupman 180); contrā lēgem, against a law; lēge, by law (Traupman 195).

Other words

  • jūs, jūris n. — law as a whole; right

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Verr. 2.1.109: jūs cīvīle (Lewis & Short); Cic. Off. 1.33: summum jūs summa injūria; Traupman 195; Traupman 338

    The law as a body, and what is right by it: contrā jūs, against the law (Traupman 195); jūs cīvīle, the civil law, as a subject of study.

  • fās (indecl.) — divine law, what is right in the eyes of the gods

    also used · classical · Traupman 338

    Opposed to jūs, human law (Lewis & Short); fās est, it is lawful, it is right.

Examples

  • plūsque ibi bonī mōrēs valent quam alibī bonae lēgēs

    and good customs count for more there than good laws elsewhereTac. Germ. 19.5

  • ollīs salūs populī suprēma lēx estō

    for them the safety of the people shall be the highest lawCic. Leg. 3.8

  • ex quō illud ‘summum jūs summa injūria’ factum est jam trītum sermōne prōverbium

    hence “the strictest law is the greatest injustice” has become a common proverbCic. Off. 1.33

  • lēge

    in accordance with the lawTraupman 179

  • secundum lēgem

    according to the lawTraupman 178

  • lēgem perferre

    to pass a lawTraupman 179

  • lēgem jubēre

    to ratify a bill (of the people voting it into law)Traupman 180

  • lēgem antīquāre

    to reject a billTraupman 180

  • voluntās lēgis

    the spirit of the lawTraupman 180

  • contrā jūs (contrā lēgem)

    against the law (against a particular law)Traupman 195

  • lēgem violāre

    to break the lawTraupman 195

  • lēgem exercēre

    to enforce the lawTraupman 195; cf. Suet. Caes. 43: lēgem sūmptuāriam (Lewis & Short s.v. exerceō)

  • summō jūre cum aliquō agere

    to throw the book at someone (literally “to deal with him by the full rigour of the law”)Traupman 197; cf. Cic. Off. 1.33: summō jūre agere (Lewis & Short s.v. agō)

  • Spērō jūdicem summō jūre cum istīs āctūrum esse.

    I hope the judge throws the book at them.Traupman 192

  • lēgem pertulit

    he got the law passedLiv. 33.46 (Lewis & Short s.v. perferō)

  • rogātiōnem (lēgem) perferre

    to pass a bill (a law)Traupman 357

  • lēgem (rogātiōnem) antīquāre

    to reject a billTraupman 370
